scope: Disposition of every entry in the 0.3 changelog as retrieved on 29 October 2026. Done records implementation of that entry with the stated evidence and limits; it does not claim full specification or Guides conformance.

changes.notes: Scope descriptions come from listed OpenAPI OAuth schemes first, then auth.scopes, following our precedence reading for upstream audit item 31. The Company's wording is preserved in discovery information and sign-in cards. The regression exercises conflicting descriptions and the auth.scopes fallback. The validator cannot read OpenAPI descriptions, so it warns about undescribed scopes only for Companies that list no OpenAPI API.

changes.change: Sign-in types from the OAuth server metadata
changes.notes: Direct and Device Sign-In come from grant_types_supported; Mediated Sign-In from its extension. Any scope in scopes_supported may be requested by Direct or Device.

Discovery ignores unknown hint fields and maps an unfamiliar changes value to irreversible. Scope information and sign-in cards show hints in plain words. Missing hints default to irreversible with personal data, following the Guides and our scope-hint reading in docs/readings.md; this is a documented choice for the conflict in upstream audit item 30, not a specification MUST. The Company's scope description is preserved; test/poppy-model-policy.test.ts checks the actual model-facing discovery result.
Section numbers in code, comments, the protocol log and the mock's checks follow 0.3 (4 OAuth, 5 Sessions, 6 web, 7 APIs, 8 conversations, 9 task coverage).

Every resource request carries a Poppy-Session JWT signed for it; plain refresh and access tokens; DPoP only when the issuer lists algorithms; invalid_session starts a new Session once. Session Tokens, the jwt-bearer grant and session_id are gone (decision 37). MCP servers get Bearer tokens for their url.
One agent acts for each User here, so Session JWTs carry no agent_id. sessionJwt can carry one; the mock checks that a Session's Agent ID never changes (session-jwt.sub-changed).

changes.change: Session JWTs signed with delegated keys
changes.notes: Delegations (pap-delegation+jwt, cnf.jwk, no User or Company) last 4 hours from an iat rounded down to the hour and are renewed 10 minutes early; one delegated key per User ID per Company.
A second account at the same Company gets a new Session (sid), even after signing out of the first: the used_account column remembers the account a Session was used with.

changes.change: Browsers join a Session with an authorized one-time code
changes.notes: GET the browser-session page, authorize its code at {endpoint}/authorize with the Session header and token, then the browser posts the form; the code never reaches the model. The browser assertion is gone.

Credential-free excluded-task documents are cached raw and filtered for each Company. Discovery delivers exclusions and validated web alternatives directly to the User, independent of model repetition. Semantic task matching and the model's choice to try a suitable alternative still require model judgment.

Accepts 202 or 200 with a filtered alternative, reports once per task and never an excluded one. Alternatives reach the User directly. Recognizable credentials, contact details and personal identifiers are refused before sending; arbitrary personal statements cannot be fully classified.
Tokens, Session JWTs, keys, codes, verifiers, device codes and one-time codes never reach the model, the transcript or the logs (decision 31; src/log.ts).

Our keys sign client assertions and delegations in our own Worker, which already acts for the User, so blind signing would hide nothing from us; ES256 only. The validator accepts PS384 keys and the mock accepts PS384 client assertions and delegations.

Operations 2 is implemented on API, MCP and conversation channels. Unknown outcomes hold all further writes at the Company until the authenticated User records a checked outcome; the original uncertain receipt remains durable. We do not automatically resend uncertain writes. API 202, approved 5xx and conversation acknowledgements remain uncertain. Terms lifecycle tests cover both API and MCP; actual Chromium journeys check clicks, effects and recovery.

changes.change: Mediated Sign-In is an extension grant
changes.notes: The grant at the token endpoint, code_required then sign_in_id and one_time_code alone; reserved field names are refused; credentials go only to the issuer's token endpoint.
chooseSignInType prefers Direct, then Device, then Mediated.
Refresh token and access token in code and on the page; some stable ids (account-token.* checks, poppy_accounts) keep their old names.

changes.change: Discovery redirects end at the well-known path
changes.notes: poppy-redirect-path: a document whose last URL isn't exactly /.well-known/poppy.json with no query is refused.
Nothing to remove on our side: the behaviours stay (caching by headers, refresh tokens only at the token and revocation endpoints).

changes.change: The issuer from protected resource metadata
changes.notes: The issuer comes from https://{domain}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource; auth.issuer only picks among several.
The issuer must list https://{organization.domain}; device links are checked against its entries' hosts.
An unknown API type is skipped by the client and is an informational note in the validator, no longer an error.

changes.change: Tokens for one service from protected resource metadata
changes.notes: Reads service metadata and requests its resource. invalid_token/resource_metadata triggers one safe credential-free refetch, revalidating URI, issuer, host and resource. Default/service-specific audiences can change both ways; an explicit MCP resource remains its exact URL. Withdrawal during refetch prevents dispatch.
The client metadata lists Operations 2 only; Mediated Sign-In is recognized from its grant.
The validator accepts http://127.0.0.1 and http://[::1] redirect URIs; our Worker has no use for one.
One-minute client assertions with iat and a 128-bit jti, aud the issuer as a single string.
We still follow the moved advice (no markup in text, complete messages only, one-time codes kept out of the model).
Direct Sign-In is preferred when offered; device links are shown only on the Company's hosts.
Sign-out revokes every refresh token held for the account; the Session continues signed out with the same sid.
A missing scope means the scopes requested (grantedScope); no signed_in or session_id.

Discovery describes Company scopes, preferring OpenAPI descriptions to auth.scopes. Missing hints are supplied conservatively as irreversible with personal data. The User approves sign-in; requesting the smallest sufficient scope set remains model-guided and is not claimed as a universal behavioral proof.
One random User ID per User per Company, never derived from personal information.
/poppy/client.json is served at exactly its URL; the validator refuses a redirect there.
A 401 with no error code and a scope is handled as insufficient_scope; conversations' authorization events too.
429 with Retry-After is respected everywhere through the shared CompanyLimiter.

changes.change: Only the Personal Agent's browser joins a Session
changes.notes: Only the agent's FetchBrowser joins, using its private per-User/Session cookie jar. The regression keeps an ordinary User visit signed out, verifies the joined agent sees its account, and checks join material never reaches tool output or cards. Existing tests isolate two Users and two Sessions. This restores an explicit MUST; it changes no wire format.
Nothing to send; the model reads the page's error and can ask for the scope.

Our messages carry author.type (test/poppy-0.3.test.ts). A Company author's name reaches model notices and the Direct Conversation frame; its image is not fetched. UI regressions in test/ui/company-author-display.test.tsx verify Company attribution and render the name as text, without interpreting HTML.

Unknown status and responder values become working and human, respectively. The regression supplies unfamiliar values on conversation creation and in later event reads, checking both the returned state and the stored conversation.
Reports carry task and description only; the mock records a report with kind (feedback.kind).

changes.change: Verifying the user by sign-in in conversations
changes.notes: The tool boundary withholds recognizable credentials and replies to explicit Company verification requests with a fixed request for an authorization event, once per Company prompt. The chosen prompt and message identity survive replay, restart and a lost answer. Later verification prompts in the same conversation can request authorization again. Real faux-model negative and ordinary-task positive controls pass. This recognizes bounded patterns, not every language or paraphrase.

changes.change: Authorization servers without client ID metadata documents
changes.notes: A Company that registers agents by client_id gets ours at /poppy/client.json; the mock's requireRegistration tests invalid_client.

changes.change: API descriptions and one feedback channel
changes.notes: Feedback goes only to feedback.endpoint through poppy_feedback, never an API operation.
